title: Customer Lifetime Value Projection
description:
A `customer_orders` table holds purchase history per customer. Compute the **projected 3-year Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)** for each customer using the formula:

> `CLV = avg_order_value × orders_per_year × 3`

where `orders_per_year = total_orders / MAX(lifespan_days, 365) * 365` and `lifespan_days = last_order_date − first_order_date`.

**Table: customer_orders**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| order_id | INT |
| customer_id | INT |
| order_date | DATE |
| order_value | NUMERIC(10,2) |

Output columns: `customer_id`, `avg_order_value`, `orders_per_year`, `projected_3yr_clv`. Order by `projected_3yr_clv` DESC.
solution_sql: WITH customer_stats AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, SUM(order_value) AS total_revenue, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value, MIN(order_date) AS first_order, MAX(order_date) AS last_order, GREATEST(MAX(order_date) - MIN(order_date), 365) AS lifespan_days FROM customer_orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id, ROUND(avg_order_value::NUMERIC, 2) AS avg_order_value, ROUND((total_orders / (lifespan_days / 365.0))::NUMERIC, 2) AS orders_per_year, ROUND((avg_order_value * (total_orders / (lifespan_days / 365.0)) * 3)::NUMERIC, 2) AS projected_3yr_clv FROM customer_stats ORDER BY projected_3yr_clv DESC

test_cases.description: Projected 3-year CLV ranked highest to lowest

hints: Use GREATEST(last_order_date - first_order_date, 365) to ensure the minimum observation window is 1 year — without this, single-purchase customers with a 0-day lifespan would divide by zero and inflate CLV artificially.

Chain two CTEs: the first computes per-customer stats (total orders, avg order value, date range). The second applies the CLV formula. All customers in this dataset have a lifespan ≤ 365 days, so GREATEST clips to 365 and orders_per_year equals total_orders.
explanation: CLV = avg_order_value × purchase_frequency × projected_years. Purchase frequency (orders_per_year) is total orders divided by the observation window in years, with a minimum of 1 year to avoid artificially inflating one-time purchasers. The GREATEST(..., 365) guard caps the denominator. Because all customers in this dataset have a lifespan shorter than a year, orders_per_year equals total_orders, simplifying CLV to total_revenue × 3. Customer 2 has the highest CLV (4650) due to large average orders (516.67) despite fewer orders than customer 3. Customer 3 has many small orders (avg 90) giving it the lowest CLV despite the highest purchase frequency. This model is foundational in subscription businesses and e-commerce retention strategy.
